# Nova API — one pipeline

The operations Nova tags `public` under `/api/pipelines/{id}`. Generated from `reference-src/nova-openapi.json`.

## GET /api/pipelines/\{namespace\}/\{name\}

Operation id `pipelines_get`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_get", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_get`.

One pipeline: the list fields, the latest 20 runs, and the resource's `params`, `retries` and `options` (defaults filled in when a field is absent, so the edit dialog can prefill). A pipeline whose DAG does not exist yet answers 200 with `loaded: false` and `state: "loading"`. A pipeline of another group answers 404. History of a deleted pipeline is not offered in this version: without the resource the answer is 404.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | Yes | Pipeline name |
| `namespace` | path | string | Yes | The Pipeline's namespace (Nova's own) |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The pipeline, its latest runs, params, retries and options |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `404` | No such pipeline for this caller |
| `502` | The scheduler or the cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured |

## PUT /api/pipelines/\{namespace\}/\{name\}

Operation id `pipelines_update`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_update", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_update`.

Change a pipeline Nova created (`app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: stardelt-nova`) and nothing else. A statement pipeline's body carries `sql`; a notebook pipeline's carries `notebook` (`{ name, objectVersion, params }`), and an update never changes which of the two it is: `sql` on a notebook pipeline is 400 `this pipeline runs a notebook`, a notebook on a statement pipeline 400 `this pipeline runs a statement`, and both or neither 400 `give a statement, a notebook, a dbt run or a quality run`. A task-list pipeline's body carries `tasks` and replaces the whole list; any other body on a task list is 409 `this pipeline has several tasks; change it in its file and deploy again`, and `tasks` on a statement or notebook pipeline is 400 `this pipeline runs a statement` / `this pipeline runs a notebook`. The body describes the whole editable state: an omitted `schedule` removes it, an omitted `params` removes the table, an omitted option keeps its default, and a notebook body's file name, version and parameters replace the task's `config`. Refusals: a pipeline the caller cannot see 404, and one it can see but may not change — a viewer (`spec.viewers`) — 403 `only the owner group may change this pipeline`; a pipeline Nova did not write, or one whose task shape is not exactly one `run` task of kind `sql` or `notebook` 409; the statement, a parameter, a placeholder, a notebook name, a parameter value or count, or a version that is not in the store (503 without `NOVA_S3_*`, 502 when S3 does not answer), an option, the cron or the timezone as on create 400; the group's principal no longer ready 409 with the `principals` route's message; a concurrent change to the resource 409 `the pipeline changed while you edited it: reload`. A body may carry `resourceVersion` (the one `pipelines_spec` answered): when it is not the stored one, the answer is that same 409 and nothing is written; omitted, the update behaves as before. In a stage whose NOVA_STAGE_KIND is prod, a body that schedules a notebook is refused with 400 "In production a notebook comes from Git. Deploy it with a bundle." unless it carries a bundle deploy stamp (provenance, or one already on the pipeline); other stages and statement schedules are unaffected. The audit line carries the statement's length, the cron and, for a notebook, the group, the file name and the pinned version — never the statement and never a parameter value. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | Yes | Pipeline name |
| `namespace` | path | string | Yes | The Pipeline's namespace (Nova's own) |

**Request body**

| `description` | string (nullable) | No |  | One line saying what the pipeline does (`spec.description`); at most 200 characters. Omitted or blank removes the line, as the rest of the body describes the whole editable state. |  |
| `notebook` | object | No |  | The notebook, its version and its parameters for a notebook pipeline; a statement pipeline refuses it. |  |
| `notebook.connection` | string (nullable) | No |  | The `Connection` whose secret fields the task pod receives as `CONN_<NAME>_<KEY>` (the CRD's `tasks[].connection`). Omitted: the pod gets no connection variable. Nova checks the shape only; whether the connection exists, is Ready, is of this group and is in its `usableBy` is the loader's job, and its sentence is the one the task log shows. |  |
| `notebook.name` | string | Yes |  | `<group>/<name>` is the object key; the group is the pipeline's `ownerGroup`, so a notebook of another group can never be named. |  |

## DELETE /api/pipelines/\{namespace\}/\{name\}

Operation id `pipelines_delete`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_delete", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_delete`.

Delete a pipeline Nova created. Only the owner group and administrators may delete: a viewer (`spec.viewers`) answers 403 `only the owner group may change this pipeline`, and a pipeline the caller cannot see 404. A pipeline that carries `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: stardelt-nova` may be deleted: a `kubectl` or GitOps pipeline answers 409 instead. Airflow is not called — the resource is the source of truth; the DAG leaves the scheduler's default list after about 90 seconds while its history stays readable. Answers 204 with `Cache-Control: no-store`; the attempt is audited.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | Yes | Pipeline name |
| `namespace` | path | string | Yes | The Pipeline's namespace (Nova's own) |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `204` | Deleted (or already gone) |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `403` | The caller may see but not change this pipeline |
| `404` | No such pipeline for this caller |
| `409` | The pipeline is managed outside Nova |
| `502` | The cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection |

## POST /api/pipelines/\{namespace\}/\{name\}/pause

Operation id `pipelines_pause`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_pause", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_pause`.

Pause a pipeline. Idempotent: pausing a paused pipeline answers 200. Changing a pipeline is the owner group's and administrators' verb: a viewer (`spec.viewers`) may read and run it but not pause it, and answers 403 `only the owner group may change this pipeline` — a pipeline the caller cannot see stays 404. A pipeline the scheduler has not loaded answers 409. Answers the fresh `PipelineView` — the DAG as Airflow returned it after the patch — and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | Yes | Pipeline name |
| `namespace` | path | string | Yes | The Pipeline's namespace (Nova's own) |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The pipeline, now paused |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `403` | The caller may see but not change this pipeline |
| `404` | No such pipeline for this caller |
| `409` | The scheduler has not loaded this pipeline yet |
| `502` | The scheduler or the cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection, or the scheduler is not configured |

## POST /api/pipelines/\{namespace\}/\{name\}/resume

Operation id `pipelines_resume`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_resume", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_resume`.

Resume a pipeline. Idempotent: resuming a running pipeline answers 200. Changing a pipeline is the owner group's and administrators' verb: a viewer (`spec.viewers`) may read and run it but not resume it, and answers 403 `only the owner group may change this pipeline` — a pipeline the caller cannot see stays 404. A pipeline the scheduler has not loaded answers 409. Answers the fresh `PipelineView` — the DAG as Airflow returned it after the patch — and `Cache-Control: no-store`. The attempt is audited, including a refusal.

## GET /api/pipelines/\{namespace\}/\{name\}/spec

Operation id `pipelines_spec`: in Python `client.call("pipelines_spec", …)`, on the command line `stardelt api pipelines_spec`.

The editable document of one pipeline, in the shape of the body of `pipelines_create`: `name`, `ownerGroup`, a `sql` statement or a `notebook` (file name, pinned object version, parameters), a `schedule` (`cron` and `timezone`; a resource without a zone is `UTC`), the `params` table (left out when empty) and the `options` with their defaults filled in. It is built from the resource alone, so it answers while the scheduler is down. `resourceVersion` is the resource's version; `managedBy` is `nova` or `other` (kubectl or GitOps); `editable` is true only for a pipeline Nova wrote that has one `run` task of kind `sql` or `notebook`, or a task list whose every task is `sql`, `notebook` or `dbt`; an update replaces a task list whole. A pipeline that is not editable is still readable: its document then leaves out what the form cannot show. The document never holds status, annotations, a connection's secret or a token. A pipeline of another group answers 404. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | path | string | Yes | Pipeline name |
| `namespace` | path | string | Yes | The Pipeline's namespace (Nova's own) |

**Responses**

| Code | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | The document, its resource version, who manages it, and whether it is editable |
| `401` | No token to sign in with |
| `404` | No such pipeline for this caller |
| `502` | The cluster did not answer |
| `503` | No cluster connection |
